get.description:
Get list of Shopify stores connected to this account.

Implementation:
1. Retrieve all access tokens for the ACCOUNT (a team member resolves to
   their owner: stores are connected once per account, not per seat)
2. Decrypt each token to get the plaintext mega_token
3. Query Shopify database to find shops using each mega_token
4. Return aggregated list of shops found

This ensures the caller only sees shops their account owns tokens for.

What the account's calendar-backed AI tools are wired to.

Account level on purpose: a calendar is connected once per account and
serves every instance and every agent, so this answers for surfaces that
have no agent id yet (the create-agent drawer) and for the instance AI
settings page. The agent workspace gets the same payload inline on
``GET /ai/agents/{id}/actions`` and does not call this.

``instance_id`` is how the instance-level AI settings page asks. Without
it a team member resolves to themselves (resolve_account_scope only
widens for can_manage_integrations), and the booking toggle on a page
they DO have access to would claim the account has no calendar. With it,
the owner comes from the instance, the same way every other endpoint on
that page resolves it.

Never 404s on a disabled provider: "this deployment does not offer
Calendly" is exactly what the toggle needs to say, and a 404 would leave
it showing "not connected" with a connect button that cannot work.

Get message flow analytics showing sent vs received patterns

Per-conversation-partner analytics, counted off our own outbound rows.

Two defects this route used to have, both of the same shape:

* ``delivery_rate`` divided a count of delivered messages by
  ``message_count``, which counts BOTH directions. The customers who reply
  most therefore rendered as the worst delivering: one live recipient with
  52 outbound and 143 inbound messages showed 26.67% while every message we
  sent them had arrived.
* The whole route was gated on ``recipient IS NOT NULL``, so it returned an
  empty list on Instagram, web widget and messenger, where the conversation
  partner lives in recipient_bsuid / sender_bsuid. One live Instagram
  account had 1,421 conversation partners and an empty panel.

get.description:
Retrieve current logged-in user's info with database user type information.

Returns both Keycloak token claims AND database user info including:
- user_id: Database UUID
- is_agent: True if user has parent_user_id
- is_owner: True if user has no parent_user_id
- parent_user_id: If agent, the owner's user_id
- is_enabled: Whether the account is enabled
- is_affiliate_only: True for affiliate-portal-only accounts (provisioned
  at partner approval, marked by the affiliate_only sentinel role); the
  frontend lands these on /affiliate instead of the customer dashboard.
  A customer who is also an affiliate reports False and keeps the normal
  dashboard.
- is_creator: True when the account holds the Creator Marketplace creator
  role. This one CANNOT be read off the token claims: unlike `affiliate`,
  the creator role is granted as an app-managed write to the Users.roles
  column at claim time (see creator_application_service.claim_creator_account)
  and is never provisioned into Keycloak, so it never appears in
  realm_access. Without this flag the frontend has no way to tell a
  creator from any other customer, which is why the creator portal had no
  nav entry at all and was reachable only by typing the URL.

This allows the frontend to determine user type without additional API calls.

post.description:
Mark a single group message as read on both the local DB and Meta.

Per the 14 May 2026 Meta changelog, group messages do NOT honour the
"latest message implicitly marks earlier ones read" semantics that
direct DMs use — each ``wa_message_id`` in a group must be marked
individually. Frontend should call this per visible/intersected
group message.

Behavior:
* Stamps ``business_read_at`` + ``business_read_by`` on the Messages
  row owned by this instance + user + group_id.
* Pushes the read receipt to Meta's Cloud API via
  ``meta_api_client.mark_message_as_read``. Failures are logged and
  swallowed — local read state has already succeeded.

FlowNodeSchema.title: FlowNodeSchema
FlowNodeSchema.description:
Individual flow node definition.

Supported node types:
- start: Entry point for flow (trigger configuration)
- action: Send plain text message
- template_action: Send WhatsApp template message
- condition: Conditional branching. Routes via a 'true'/'false' branch
    (the outgoing edge whose sourceHandle matches the branch). Selected by
    node data 'source':
      * (unset)/'value' — legacy scalar compare: conditionType
        'equals'|'contains'|'not_equals' over templated leftValue/rightValue.
      * 'field' — compare a contact custom field: key (str), op
        'equals'|'not_equals'|'contains'|'gt'|'lt'|'exists'|'empty',
        value (templated; ignored for exists/empty). Read from the contact's
        custom_fields JSONB.
      * 'segment' — "contact is (not) in segment": segment_id (UUID), op
        'in'|'not_in' (default 'in'). Cheap single-contact EXISTS against
        the segment's compiled filters (never resolves the whole segment).
- delay: Smart Delay — pause flow execution and resume after a configured
    duration via a Celery countdown (same pause/resume machinery as
    wait_for_reply, but timer-only with no early "replied" path). Resumes
    from the node AFTER the delay. (node data: delayValue int, delayType
    'seconds'|'days', optional delayCondition 'unconditional'|'inactive';
    forward-compatible fallback: duration int + unit 'minutes'|'hours'|'days';
    default 1s, clamp: 1s min – 604800s / 7 days max)
- block_action: Block contact from receiving messages
- interactive_buttons: Send interactive message with buttons (1-3 buttons)
- label_action: Assign or unassign labels to/from contact
- contact_update: Add a note/update to the contact's history
- set_custom_field: Set or clear a contact custom field. Goes through
    ContactCustomFieldService (same validation/coercion + unknown-key
    rejection as the contacts UI). (node data: key str (required), value
    (templated; required unless clear), clear bool — when true the key is
    removed instead of set). Failures log + continue (never abort the flow).
- cooldown: Terminal node — prevents contact from re-triggering flow for a
    configurable duration (node data: duration int, unit 'minutes'|'hours'|'days')
- wa_notify: Send a WhatsApp template message to one or more configured recipients
    (e.g. business owner, manager) — NOT the flow contact. Uses template messages
    because there is no 24-hour messaging window with arbitrary recipients.
    (node data: recipients list of {phone, label}, templateName, language,
    headerParams, bodyParams, buttonParams)
- wait_for_reply: Pause flow execution for a configurable duration. If the contact
    replies during the wait the execution is completed early. If the timeout expires
    without a reply, execution resumes from the next node via a Celery countdown task.
    (node data: duration int, unit 'minutes'|'hours'|'days', defaults: 1 hour,
    clamp: 60s min – 259200s / 3 days max)

on ``InstanceMeResponse``, and ``derive_connection_status`` deliberately
excludes it, so nothing else in the payload could have carried the outcome.

``InstanceMeResponse``: the list, get and update endpoints never migrate
anything, and a ``migration_moved: false`` on every row there would be
noise at best and a claim at worst.

Same vocabulary as ``POST /facebook/whatsapp/onboard`` so the frontend has
one shape to branch on. All three are NULL when no migration was requested.
